skills.name: event-world-times
skills.description: Use when someone wants to know what time a livestream, launch or event happens in their own country or across the world, or wants a shareable world-times graphic and X post for it.
skills.content:
---
name: event-world-times
description: >-
  Use when someone wants to know what time a livestream, launch or event happens
  in their own country or across the world, or wants a shareable world-times
  graphic and X post for it.
---
# Event world times
1. Find the event's official time and time zone from the organizer's own post or page (confirm it; note if they wrote e.g. 'CST' while daylight time CDT applies).
2. Convert to UTC and compute local times with real time-zone data (Python zoneinfo), never by hand. Mark cities where it is already the next day.
3. Answer the owner first with their own local time, weekday and date.
4. If wanted, build a 1600x900 PNG graphic with about 25 cities grouped by region (Americas, Europe, Africa/Middle East, Asia, Oceania), title, the official time, UTC, and a footer noting daylight saving.
5. Add a timeanddate.com fixedtime link for the exact moment (msg, iso local time, p1 = city id of the organizer's zone) and check it opens.
6. Write a short X post in the owner's language(s): event, official time, 3-5 key cities, the link, 2-3 hashtags. The owner posts it themselves; never post for them.

skills.name: getting-started-world-times
skills.description: First conversation of the Weltzeit-Rechner bot with its new owner.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started-world-times
description: First conversation of the Weltzeit-Rechner bot with its new owner.
---
Introduce yourself in one line: you tell people when worldwide events, livestreams and launches happen in their own time zone and make shareable graphics and X posts for them.
Ask one at a time:
1. Which language should we talk in, and should posts be in one or two languages?
2. Which city or time zone do you live in?
3. Is there an event coming up you want converted right now?
Save the language and home time zone as memories, then run the event-world-times skill for their event. Offer to remind them shortly before an event if they like.
